Thresholds guessed where the brief has none: a 48-hour hold counted in calendar hours; three items includes items on loan only, not pending reservations; damage charge capped at replacement value.

open_questions.text: Fees vs lending competing criteria: fees wants a balance to block borrowing the moment it accrues, lending wants a paid-at-the-desk cash fee to unblock check-out in the same visit. With a synchronous read both hold only if cash is recorded before check-out - confirm that desk order.
Is a query's producer the context that asks or the one that answers? The pre-fill read membership-current (producer lending) as contradicting R1 (membership upstream). Connect should say.

canvases.name: Membership
canvases.purpose: Membership decides who is a member, at which rate, and until when: a resident applies, the coordinator approves a concession, the annual fee is paid and a 12-month membership starts; nightly, expired memberships lapse. It answers 'is this membership current?' for lending. It does not decide who may borrow (lending) and holds no fee balance (fees).
canvases.domain_roles_rationale: Owns the membership aggregate and moves it applied -> started -> lapsed on commands from the member, the coordinator and the clock; the only human-in-the-loop step is concession approval. Card capture for the joining fee reuses fees' Stripe adapter.

ubiquitous_language.definition: a person with contact details, a member number, a rate (standard or concession) and a term that expires
A member's 12-month right to borrow, started when the annual fee is paid

business_decisions: A membership starts the day the annual fee is received and expires 12 months later; on the nightly run an expired membership lapses and the member is no longer current.
The concession rate (GBP 15) applies only after the coordinator has approved the uploaded proof; until then the standard fee (GBP 40) is due.
A lapsed member may still return items and pay fees (understand Q1, assumed); only new borrowing needs a current membership.

canvases.name: Inventory
canvases.purpose: Inventory decides which tools exist as kinds and which physical items belong to each, and whether each item is fit to lend: volunteers add tools, tag donated items, inspect, repair and retire them. It tells lending which items may be offered (G1 indirectly: a fit item is a returnable item) and tells fees when an inspection fails after a loan. It does not hold availability (lending) or charge anyone (fees).
canvases.domain_roles_rationale: Owns the tool and item aggregates; every command comes from the maintenance volunteer; one manual policy reacts to a damaged return. No external system.

ubiquitous_language.definition: a catalogue kind with replacement value, safety notes and induction flag; owns its items
one asset-tagged physical unit with a condition and a lifecycle (fit, in maintenance, retired)
A maintenance volunteer's safety and condition check of an item; pass or fail

business_decisions: An item returned with damage noted is inspected before it can be lent again; until the inspection passes it is not fit.
An item that fails inspection is either repaired (back to fit) or retired; a retired item leaves the catalogue view, keeps its loan history, and is published to lending as item-retired.
Every item belongs to exactly one tool kind, whose replacement value caps any late or damage fee for it.

Every item has a tool kind and an asset tag (data completeness 100%).

canvases.name: Lending
canvases.purpose: Lending decides who may borrow what, and until when: it holds reservations, checks items out and back in at the Saturday desk, renews once, reminds, and marks loans overdue, so that 90% of loans come back on time (G1). It owns the borrow decision (membership current, balance zero, no overdue, fewer than three out) and asks membership and fees for the two facts it does not hold. It does not know a member's contact details (membership), what an item is worth or whether it is fit (inventory), or what anyone owes (fees).
canvases.domain_roles_rationale: Owns the reservation and loan aggregates and moves them through hold -> checked out -> due -> overdue -> returned on commands from members, desk volunteers and the clock; both pivotal events of the storm are its. Clock and email are adapters inside it, not a gateway role.

ubiquitous_language.definition: A 48-hour hold on an available item for one member
One item in one member's hands from check-out to return, due in 14 days, renewable once by 7
The day a loan must be returned by; the day after it the loan is overdue
a lendable unit with an availability (available, reserved, on loan); condition is not modelled here
a borrower identified by member number with a standing (may borrow or not) - no contact details

business_decisions: A member may check an item out only if the membership is current, the fee balance is zero, no loan of theirs is overdue, and fewer than three of their loans are open; any one failing blocks the check-out with the reason (decompose D1, A10).
A loan is due 14 days after check-out; it may be renewed exactly once, by 7 days, and only if no other member holds a reservation on that item.
A reservation holds an available item for 48 hours (calendar, A10); when the hold passes the item is available again and a check-out against the expired hold is refused.
A loan whose due date has passed at the nightly run is overdue: the member cannot borrow more, and fees is told (loan-overdue) so accrual starts; the return (item-returned) stops it.
An item that inventory has retired or failed is never offered for reservation, even if it is physically on the shelf.

canvases.name: Fees
canvases.purpose: Fees decides what a member owes and records how it is paid: it accrues GBP 1 per overdue item per day (capped at the item's replacement value), takes damage charges from the coordinator, applies waivers, and collects payment by card through Stripe or cash at the desk, so that 80% of fees are paid within 30 days (G2). It answers 'what is the balance?' for lending. It does not decide who may borrow (lending) or what an item is worth (inventory).
canvases.domain_roles_rationale: Owns the fee-account ledger and moves it through accrue -> charge -> pay -> waive; it is also the one place Stripe is called, so it carries the gateway role: idempotency keys, declines and late webhooks are its design problem (CC1).

ubiquitous_language.definition: GBP 1 per item per overdue day, capped at the item's replacement value
What a member owes in late and damage fees; must be zero to borrow
an account holder with a balance in pence; nothing else about the person
A member's running ledger of late fees, damage charges, payments and waivers; its balance is what the member owes

business_decisions: While a loan is overdue, each nightly run adds GBP 1 per item to the member's balance until the item is returned or the total for that loan reaches the item's replacement value (cap per loan, discover Q2 assumed).
A damage charge is set by the coordinator only, after a failed inspection, and never exceeds the item's replacement value.

A payment attempt is recorded as pending before Stripe is called with the attempt id as idempotency key; the outcome (paid or declined) is recorded once, and a later webhook with the same key changes nothing (CC1).
A cash payment at the desk is recorded by the volunteer as fee-paid with method cash; no Stripe call.
Only the coordinator may waive; a waiver records who and why.

quality_attributes.requirement: The borrow rule is evaluated once, atomically with the check-out
quality_attributes.scenario: Two desk volunteers check out the same member's third and fourth item within a second -> exactly one succeeds and the other is refused with 'three items out'.

quality_attributes.requirement: Nightly overdue marking never misses a loan and never marks a returned one
quality_attributes.scenario: The nightly run is restarted mid-way -> after the rerun every loan past due is overdue exactly once and no returned loan is.

quality_attributes.requirement: Check-out completes in under 2 s including the two in-process reads
quality_attributes.scenario: Saturday 10:00 desk peak, 5 volunteers checking out concurrently -> each check-out is acknowledged within 2 s at p95 (I3: under five minutes per transaction).

quality_attributes.requirement: A payment attempt charges the card at most once
quality_attributes.scenario: Stripe times out after charging and the member retries -> the same attempt id is reused, Stripe returns the original outcome, one fee-paid is recorded (C1, CC1).

notes_for_downstream.text: Lending's eligibility check needs two driven ports (MembershipStatus, FeeBalance) answered in-process by membership and fees; do not model them as repositories over another module's tables.

plain_words.what: We wrote one page per part of the system (a bounded-context canvas) saying what it decides, for whom, which messages go in and out, and the rules it must keep.
plain_words.decided: 4 canvases. Lending keeps the borrow rule in one place with 5 rules; fees keeps the money rules with 5, including 'charge a card at most once'. 4 quality demands, all on lending and fees.
plain_words.assumed: Thresholds nobody confirmed: a 48-hour hold in calendar hours, three items counts only items out, a lapsed member can still return and pay.
plain_words.riskiest: If the borrow rule's four facts are not all true at the same instant at the desk (cash paid then borrowed in one visit), the system will refuse or allow borrowing wrongly and volunteers will stop trusting it.
